Pylon’s API is available in two regions. Use the base URL that matches where your Pylon tenant is hosted:
- US region: https://api.usepylon.com
- EU region: https://api.eu.usepylon.com
Both regions use the same API endpoints and authentication. Configure your integration to use the region where your Pylon tenant is hosted.

results.title: Set up the Pylon MCP server
results.snippet:
- **Pylon MCP** — listed as plain **Pylon** in your catalog. C1 registers Pylon’s own hosted MCP server (`mcp.usepylon.com`) as a downstream server C1 governs. Authentication is always per-user OAuth using dynamic client registration (DCR) — Pylon’s hosted MCP server doesn’t support a bearer token or API key, so there’s no integration to create in Pylon first. Tool calls run with the connected user’s own Pylon seat permissions.
- **Pylon API** — C1 hosts its own MCP server that translates Pylon’s REST API into tools. Authentication is a single shared bearer token (an API token generated in Pylon), so every tool call reaches Pylon as one shared identity.
| | Pylon MCP | Pylon API |
|---|---|---|
| **Who hosts the MCP server** | Pylon | C1 |
| **Authentication** | Per-user OAuth with dynamic client registration (DCR) only — no bearer token or API key option | Bearer token (API token) only — no OAuth option |
| **Access scoping** | The connected user’s own Pylon seat and role permissions — not independently scoped | Whatever the API token’s seat can reach in Pylon |

results.title: How do I create a Pylon API token?
results.snippet:
To create a Pylon API token, sign in as a user with permission to manage API tokens, then open **Settings → API Tokens**. If you do not see that page, ask a workspace admin to create the token or update your access.
1. Open **Settings → API Tokens**.
2. Select **Create**.
3. Enter a token name, then finish creation.
4. Copy the token immediately and store it in a secure location. Pylon only shows the full token value once.
Use the token to authenticate Pylon API requests with a Bearer header:
- `Authorization: Bearer <token>`
If you need read-only access, a workspace admin should choose an appropriate role for the token when creating it.

results.title: API conventions | Pylon
results.snippet:
How Pylon's API handles IDs, timestamps, pagination, search filters, updates, files, and slugs
These rules apply across Pylon's API. The [API reference](https://docs.usepylon.com/pylon-docs/developer/api/api-reference) lists each endpoint's parameters; this page explains how they behave.
## Requests and responses
- Send request bodies as JSON with `Content-Type: application/json`. The one exception is [`POST /attachments`](https://docs.usepylon.com/pylon-docs/developer/api/conventions#upload-a-file), which takes `multipart/form-data`.
- Successful responses put the result in `data` and include a `request_id`. List and search responses also include `pagination`.
- Unknown fields are ignored, not rejected. A misspelled field name is silently dropped, so check the field names in the reference.
- Sending `null` for an optional field is the same as leaving it out.

results.title: Connecting to the Pylon MCP Server
results.snippet:
The Pylon MCP server at [https://mcp.usepylon.com](https://mcp.usepylon.com) provides AI tools access to your Pylon data. It uses OAuth authentication with your Pylon account.
The application you connect to Pylon's MCP will only have access to data you would have access to in Pylon, and will read and write on behalf of you.
## Common Clients
### Claude Code
```plaintext
claude mcp add pylon --transport http https://mcp.usepylon.com/
```
Then, in Claude Code, run the `/mcp` command and select the `pylon` MCP to authenticate.
### Claude Desktop and Web
In "Admin Settings", add a custom connector named "Pylon" with URL `https://mcp.usepylon.com/`
Leave "OAuth Client ID" and "OAuth Client Secret" blank.
Navigate to "Settings > Connectors" and click the "Connect" button next to the Pylon MCP to authenticate.

### Cursor
Add to your Cursor MCP settings:
`~/.cursor/mcp.json` :
```plaintext
{ "mcpServers": { ... "pylon": { "url": "https://mcp.usepylon.com/" } ... } }
```
Navigate to "Cursor Settings > Tools & MCP" and click "Connect" next to the Pylon MCP to authenticate.

You can connect ChatGPT to Pylon in two ways. The fastest is Pylon’s native ChatGPT app: install it from Settings > Plugins in ChatGPT (some older views, including very old iOS or Android apps, show Apps instead of Plugins) and sign in with your Pylon account. You can also add the Pylon MCP server to ChatGPT as a custom MCP server. Either way, ChatGPT authenticates with OAuth and uses tools that read or write the same data your user can already see in Pylon.

- A Pylon workspace on a plan that includes the Pylon MCP server (listed on every plan in [Features by tier](https://www.usepylon.com/pricing)).
- A Pylon user with the **MCP Access** permission, which the standard Member and Admin roles include.

results.title: Pylon
results.snippet:
`Pylon` connects an agent to [Pylon](https://www.usepylon.com)’s hosted MCP server so it can search, read, create, and update support issues, look up and update accounts, and look up contacts as the signed-in user.

accDescr: Inside your agent, the model calls tools of the Pylon capability, prefixed pylon_, and gets their results. Your auth function gives the capability a token for each run. The capability sends tools/call with an OAuth Bearer token to the Pylon MCP server at mcp.usepylon.com, which rejects a Pylon REST API token, and with read_only=True it drops the tools not marked read-only.

You need a Pylon Member or Admin seat with the `MCP Access` role; Viewer and Integration users cannot sign in. Pylon MCP takes an OAuth access token. Pylon REST API tokens do not work with it.
Your application gets one by running the standard MCP authorization flow: the server names its authorization server and supports dynamic client registration, so any MCP OAuth client library can sign the user in. Store the token it returns and pass it as `auth` or `PYLON_ACCESS_TOKEN`.

from pydantic_ai_harness import Pylon
